why_trail.why: The frozen field group is a contract to fill, not design. The one design decision left to me is WHERE the composer's snapshot lands, and the handoff's exclusions and the gate's structural anchor (struct:episode_capture.mechanical_fields) pull in slightly different directions; question sent to commander-305b, proceeding on the reading that 'seam logic' means g1's ratified decisions (start/reopen, write-if-absent, fail-soft-not-silent) rather than the file. The real risk is not shape but sourcing: validate_delta is presence-only, so every field needs a NON-DEFAULT run proving the composer tracks engine state instead of returning a constant.

project is sourced from repository TOPOLOGY (parent of git rev-parse --git-common-dir) rather than from the work-area helper, because those answer different questions and the field wants topology. The measured red proof is the load-bearing part: on the broken durable_root formula the plain-checkout test PASSES and only the linked-worktree-under-active-epic-lease test fails, which is precisely how this defect would have shipped. Refusal on a non-repo is deliberate - there is no visible-failure channel here the way rev:null is for the manifest, so a plausible fallback would be silent poison.

The composer returns a PARTIAL dict by design: a field it cannot source honestly is absent, never defaulted. That is what makes the tests an oracle where validate_delta is not - three of the thirteen assert ABSENCE (role without a lease, project outside a repo, the step-scoped group on a fully terminal checklist), and a constant composer fails those as surely as it fails the tracking ones. spine-step imports checklist_engine.active_id through a lazy _engine() accessor because checklist_engine imports this module; a top-level import would close the cycle. artifact-ref takes the step's own git-change-policy when it declares one, else the engine's default staged mode; [] is a real answer and None (refusal) is reserved for a git failure.

Two sourcing decisions worth stating. reopens comes from the JOURNAL, not the why_trail, because reopen appends a why-marker for the target AND every cascaded downstream gate - counting markers would report reopens against a gate nobody reopened; the journal records only the verb's actual --id. And because the seam is handed a DIRECTORY, not a path, find_spine_path IDENTIFIES the checklist by matching work_id AND items against each *.json.journal's own file (this repo's own work area holds spine.json and execute.json under one work_id, so work_id alone is not enough) and refuses on zero or multiple matches rather than guessing. failed-commands counts superseded evidence deliberately: reopen supersedes evidence to stop it re-satisfying a gate, which is a claim about gate satisfaction, not about what happened.

The counter is ARMED by claim rather than created on first refusal, and that is the whole design. Without arming, absence would be ambiguous between 'no refusals yet' and 'this file predates the counter', and the composer would have to choose between a fabricated 0 and refusing a field that is genuinely 0 - both wrong. Arming makes 0 a real reading and absence a real reading. It also follows that an UNARMED checklist does not start counting on its first refusal: writing 1 onto a run whose true total may be five is exactly the plausible-wrong-number this field must never carry. Run-scoped rather than step-scoped is a deliberate departure from rework_count, stated in both the code and the schema: a refusal does not always name a task.

Wiring the snapshot at the seam exposed a defect in the adjudicated sourcing that only shows up HERE: the journal sidecar is written by main() AFTER the verb returns, so at the moment the seam fires the in-flight verb has no journal line - and at a run's FIRST mutating verb there is no journal file at all. A journal-only reopens is therefore permanently unobtainable at exactly the moment the snapshot is taken; measured, not reasoned (validate_delta rejected the first snapshot with 'create.mechanical.reopens: must be a non-negative integer', and reopens was the ONLY missing field). Resolved by reconciling two independent engine-written witnesses of the same event - the journal, and the rework_count that only reopen increments - and taking the larger, which is corroboration rather than a fallback because both can only UNDER-count and neither can over-count. That also settles the reopens-vs-rework-count scoping the convergence flagged as inferred: reopens is RUN-scoped and rework-count STEP-scoped, which is what makes them two facts rather than one number written twice. Flagged to the commander as a deviation-with-reason from the literal handoff table.

The EPISODE_STORE correction is not a wording fix: the old line promised automated capture that the store's own _validate_create forbids, so a reader of main would look for auto-created episodes that cannot exist. The rewritten line states the division the partition already implies - the mechanical half falls out of the engine, the judgment half cannot, because five non-empty assertions are required and an auto-created episode could only carry fabricated ones. Suite at 1470 passed / 2 skipped / 471 subtests against a 1436/2/471 baseline: +34, exactly the new tests, nothing else moved.
